text:
andrew: FYI ran the region-aware queue experiment across us-east/us-west (soft-affinity + opportunistic spill) this morning. some numbers looked off, posting quick dump.

mina: thanks — short summary first? p95s / kv-hit / cost delta?

andrew: short: p95 in us-east went from 45ms -> 60ms on small seq workloads, kv cache hit dropped ~7pp, cost ~+3% overall. but throughput increased a bit and tail improved on mixed-long requests.

rachel: dropping KV hit is concerning. did spillovers cause extra cache invalidations?

andrew: looks like it. profiling snippets:
```
kernel_selection: flash_attn_v2 preferred on long seqs
matmul_fp16: selected for short dense ops
kv_cache: local_hit=0.88 -> 0.81 after spill-on-overflow
queue: avg_batch_size=5.2 -> 6.8 (us-east)
queue_spill_events: 120 -> 312 (cross-zone)
```

samir: are those spill events mostly because local queue fill < X so we push to other clusters? what were the token_budget_target values?

andrew: token_budget_target was 1024 (global) with region multiplier 0.9. we had opportunistic pull to west when latency budget breached 30ms.

mina: can you paste the small YAML we used for the trial?

andrew: sure:
```
queue_policy:
  affinity: soft
  spill_threshold_ms: 30
  token_budget_target: 1024
  region_multiplier:
    us-east: 0.9
    us-west: 1.1
  spill_mode: opportunistic
```

rachel: two hypotheses: (1) opportunistic spill caused KV cache fragmentation -> lower hit; (2) kernel selection changed because of slightly different batch shape when cross-zone collocated batches mixed longer sequences.

samir: for (2) how often did kernel fallback happen? i.e., flash_attn -> slower matmul path?

andrew: fallback logs: ~4% additional fallback occurrences in us-east after experiment. mainly on 1-2 batch windows where batch contained a mix of short & long sequences.

mina: i'd try lowering region_multiplier for us-west so it doesn't lure us-east batches away, and increase token_budget_target to reduce cross-zone batching. maybe token_budget_target=1536 and set spill_threshold_ms=40 as a short test. keeps local affinity stronger.

rachel: also we can bias kernel selection by exposing a small "batch-shape hint" to the kernel picker when the queue contains high variance sequences. quick patch: set prefer_flash_when_variance=<threshold>.

andrew: noted. i'll run a canary with these changes. quick perf-bot summary from the run (auto):
```
perf-bot: run-id=2026-04-12-09:30
p50_us-east: 14ms -> 16ms
p95_us-east: 45ms -> 60ms
p99_us-east: 120ms -> 140ms
kv_hit_global: 0.88 -> 0.81
cost_delta: +3.1%
```

ops-bot: triggered alert: cross-zone egress up by 2.4GB in 10m window.

samir: 2.4GB egress matches increased spill events. the extra egress is cheap but the latency/KV impact matters. i'd rather sacrifice a bit of throughput for local KV stability.

mina: agree. propose conservative rollout plan:
- step1: increase token_budget_target to 1536 (global) and set us-west multiplier to 1.0
- step2: bump spill_threshold_ms to 40
- step3: enable batch-shape hint -> kernel picker (opt-in) in canary
- step4: collect kv_hit, kernel_fallback, p95, egress across zones for 6h

rachel: also add a micro-profiling hook to log batch shape distribution every 5m so we can confirm whether mixed batches are the root cause. minimal log size.

andrew: will run canary in us-east only, 5% traffic. initial test scheduled in 10m. /cc @perf-bot to run with flags below.

andrew: run command: `/run_bench --scope region=us-east --canary=5 --override token_budget_target=1536 spill_threshold_ms=40 batch_hint=true`

perf-bot: acknowledged. will post results in this thread.

mina: if canary improves kv_hit by >=3pp and p95 returns near baseline, we can gradually roll. otherwise we need to rethink soft-affinity semantics (maybe hard-affinity with bounded overflow).

samir: one more thought: consider local KV prefetch for sequences likely to be spilled. prefetching next token blocks into local cache when we see a spike in spill intent. that could reduce miss penalty but adds complexity. log as an action item.

rachel: agreed — add to backlog if canary fails.

andrew: thanks everyone. kicking off canary now, will paste perf-bot summary when complete. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

perf-bot: canary complete (10m median) — summary:
```
p95_us-east: 46ms (improved from 60ms)
kv_hit: 0.84 (up from 0.81, target >=0.86)
egres s: down 40% vs experiment
kernel_fallback: down to baseline +1%
cost_delta: +1.2%
notes: mixed-batch incidence reduced by ~22% due to higher token_budget
```

mina: promising. kv hit didn't fully recover but moving in right direction. suggest extend canary to 1h before wider rollout.

andrew: extending. logging batch-shape hist every 5m as rachel asked.

samir: if we still see ~+1% kernel_fallback we should evaluate adding batch-shape hint to downstream A/B.

rachel: thanks — saved this into the tuning doc. next steps captured. :white_check_mark:

andrew: will update the run notes and reopen if regressions pop up. thanks for quick triage.

mina: nice work. :thumbsup:
